newsitem.title: USA: Kennecott Copper unions ratify new deal.
newsitem.headline: Kennecott Copper unions ratify new deal.

text.p: Labor unions at Kennecott Utah Copper Corp voted to accept a new six-year labor deal, a union official confirmed.
George Stavros, business representative for the Operating Engineers Union and co-chair of the Kennecott union negotiating committee, said 704 employees voted for the new deal and 538 against.
"There is a lot of anxiety over a six year agreement," Stavros said, adding that deal, effective Friday, replaced a three-year labor package which expired on September 30.
Kennecott was hit by a brief two-day strike last week.
"We were only able to get about 3 percent wage increase per year," Stavros said.
Seventeen local unions, including the Operating Engineers took part in the vote. The United Steelworkers of America represented most of the employees.
Stavros said three local unions still have some outstanding issues to settle with the company, but these were unconnected with the overall economic package.
Stavros said union members were now working normally at Kennecott.
Company officials were not available for comment.
